newsitem.title: USA: Weather threatens U.S. shuttle launch.
newsitem.headline: Weather threatens U.S. shuttle launch.

text.p: Thunderstorms and severe weather are threatening NASA's plans to launch the space shuttle Columbia on a 16-day science mission, U.S. Air Force meterologists said on Sunday.
The shuttle had only a one-in-10 chance of getting off the launch pad as planned on Tuesday afternoon, weather officer Ed Priselac told a news conference on Sunday.

Forecasters painted a bleak picture of strong thunderstorms and rain showers through the week. Only Thursday offered the possibility of a respite from Florida's notorious summer afternoon thunderstorms.
A day into the countdown, engineers reported no major technical problems with Columbia, the oldest of NASA's four space shuttles.

The winged spaceship was scheduled to blast off at 2:37 p.m. EDT (1837 GMT) on Tuesday, but NASA officials may decide on Monday to move the shuttle's 2-1/2-hour launch window into the evening or postpone the blastoff until Wednesday.
The shuttle is making a second attempt at a 16-day research mission that was cut short in April after just five days aloft because of a troublesome power generator.
